title: Keyturn Host Protection Plan Claims Basis: Reporting a Loss and Opening a Claim
content:
A loss under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan is reported first onto the damage report register and becomes a claim only once the report is complete, so that an incomplete report never starts the appraisal clock.

### The filing window

A claim is opened only where the host reports the loss no later than the plan's filing window counted forward from the end of the trip the loss is said to have happened on. The filing window is counted in whole elapsed hours from the actual return of the vehicle recorded on the trip, never from the scheduled return and never in calendar days, and an hour counts only once it has fully elapsed. The actual return is read from the trip's own booking record for the trip the loss is attributed to, before the claim is opened, and a report made at the very last hour of the window is still inside it.

### The evidence the report carries

> Retired clause: "The report must carry at least the plan's minimum number of photographs before it becomes a claim." This clause is no longer in force and is not applied to any report.

The remainder of that provision stands: a report is completed within the plan's evidence period, counted in whole calendar days from the day the report was lodged. A report that is still short of evidence when the evidence period runs out is closed incomplete, and a fresh report on the same loss is only accepted where the filing window itself has not yet run out.

### The trip behind the loss

The trip the loss is said to have happened on must be a real trip on that vehicle that has reached the completed or settled state; a loss on a vehicle that was not on a trip is not a marketplace claim at all and belongs to the host's own motor policy. That the trip reached one of those two states is read from the trip's own booking record for that vehicle, and not from the host's description of it. Damage already recorded against an earlier trip is not claimed again on a later one, and where the same damage appears on two reports the earlier trip governs.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- A plan publishing a filing window of 48 hours: a loss reported when 47 whole hours have elapsed since the actual return is inside the window, and so is one reported when exactly 48 whole hours have elapsed; one reported when 49 whole hours have elapsed is outside it.
- A trip still running, or cancelled before it ran: no claim is opened on it at all.
